newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish "loyalist" jailed for murder threat.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish "loyalist" jailed for murder threat.

text.p: Billy Wright, a key pro-British "loyalist" hardliner feared by Northern Ireland Catholics, was jailed for eight years amid uproar in a Belfast court on Friday.
A hero to many Protestant militants and dubbed "King Rat" by the media, Wright, 36, was convicted of threatening to kill a woman who is now living under police protection in England.

Supporters shouted insults before the judge imposed the sentence on Wright, who was alleged to have threatened to shoot the woman after she had identified two men who had attacked her daughter and her boyfriend.
Wright was also convicted of perverting justice and two other men were jailed for the assault.

Wright, who defended two massacres of Catholics in an interview with an Irish newspaper in February, 1995, is viewed by security analysts as a maverick figure in his powerbase at Portadown, which is the heart of a region that has a long history of sectarian killings.

He was publicly sentenced to death by the outlawed Ulster Volunteer Force -- which like himself fiercely opposes any moves to reunite Northern Ireland with the Irish Republic -- during internal disputes last August but he defied the guerrillas and held a public rally supported by 4,000 Protestants.
In July, Wright had taken part in a prolonged angry confrontation with police blocking a banned Protestant march in Portadown.

Province-wide sectarian trouble put pressure on a two-year-old truce by loyalist guerrillas that had been shaken earlier in the year by a collapse of a 17-month ceasefire by Irish Republican Army guerrillas opposed to British rule.
